description: Library API: a partition re-initialised on the same instance (a deep tree then a flat one) is scored with the leaf network's terms. The codelength written to .tree now matches the console.
JSON modules[].codelength is filled in when the best of several trials is restored, also with --parallel-trials. It was 0 or stale.
The Miller-Madow correction is counted in bits, not nats. A module that holds the whole network has no exit codeword, and the root index codebook has one parameter less.
trials[].num_levels is the depth of the tree, not of its first branch. Differs on ragged trees.
num_levels is the depth of the tree, not of its first branch. Differs on ragged trees.
Damping strictly between 0 and 1 uses a smooth interpolation shape. Damping 0, 1 (the default) and above 1 are unchanged.
State or multilayer input: a run that would write over an input named <out-name>_states.<ext> is refused (exit 3). It used to overwrite the input.
State or multilayer input with -o network: the file is named <out-name>_states_as_physical.net, and a multilayer dump declares *Arcs.
Warns once when a .clu file repeats node ids, such as a physical .clu of a higher-order network.
A scored partition (--no-infomap with --cluster-data, or a restored best trial) includes the module-count term.
The one-level codelength and the relative savings include the module-count term for one module.
Tree, ftree and clu headers gain a '# seed' line, and the JSON tree gains seed, trials and numTrials. With --parallel-trials --print-all-trials each trial is written to its own file.
--no-overwrite and the input-overwrite check use a shard's real per-trial file names, so a collision is refused before anything is written.

Multilevel runs (not --two-level): after the recursive search, intermediate modules that do not pay for their index codebook are dissolved. Codelength drops about 0.2-0.5% on the benchmarks, and the number of top modules can grow. Skipped under --preferred-number-of-modules and an active --preferred-number-of-levels.
A one-level row in a tree file is a module of one node, whatever the row order. A bare row next to a deeper row in the same top module is refused.
Python API: multilayer networks from networkx and igraph keep their state node names (Result.state_names).
--pretty and --no-pretty warn that they have no effect.
The input fingerprint hashes the whole file, so its value changes for every input. Tree, ftree, clu and JSON output gain input, cluster data and config fingerprints. Superseded in 2.16.0 by #1172.

The aggregation loop stops at the first pass that merges nothing. This shifts the random stream, so results for a given seed can change. No average cost measured. --meta-data runs that hung now finish.
Each consolidated module keeps its own metadata collection during coarse-tune. Metadata runs optimise the right objective; air30k is about 2.5% shorter.
threads_used reports the largest OpenMP team the run started. The console Runtime line no longer prints a thread count.
Strength 0 on networks with nodes without out-links: directed runs no longer fail with degenerate flow, and undirected isolated nodes no longer get NaN flow.

Multilevel runs at the default --fast-hierarchical-solution 0, not from a seed tree deeper than two levels: when the recursive search ends above the super-level tree, that tree is reported instead. The codelength never rises. Seen mostly on state (memory) input; 1 of 60 first-order seeds changed.
Scoring a move no longer leaves rounding residue in the module's metadata. Near-ties can break differently, within 0.001%.
Parallel self-links count once in the degree sum. A node with only parallel self-links no longer gives negative flow or codelength 0.
The input fingerprint is XXH64 (the same value as xxhsum -H64). It differs from 2.15 and from #1096.
A metadata file with no records, or a directory, is refused (exit 2) instead of crashing.
Multilevel trees: each module of modules is charged its exit codeword in the correction. Best-of-N can pick a different trial.
Multilevel trees: the reported codelength includes the module-count term. Best-of-N can pick a different trial.
Node weights set through the API (add_node with a weight) are used. State input whose state ids equal the physical ids keeps its node weights.
Node weights set through the API (add_node with a weight) are used. State input whose state ids equal the physical ids keeps its node weights.
A node whose only out-link is a self-link is not dangling. Only networks with such a node change.
Markov time 1e7 and above is no longer refused for negative module flow.
Under undirdir, outdirdir, rawdir and precomputed, --recorded-teleportation has no effect and warns.

Undirected flow: a tree of three or more levels built from --cluster-data, a deep seed or a restored best trial is scored as without the option. The reported and written codelengths match, also with --no-infomap.
Under undirdir, outdirdir, rawdir and precomputed, --regularized has no effect and warns.
Bipartite input: a link that does not cross the bipartite start id is refused (exit 2).
Applies only to multilayer input. On state input it has no effect.
The dangling flow sum is reset on every run. With --parallel-trials, or a second run on one instance, results match a single serial run.
A self-link counts as one arc in the prior's average link weight. Only networks with self-links change.

When the best trial is restored (it is not the last trial, or --parallel-trials is used), module ids and node order match a one-trial run with the same seed. Two-level trees. Partition and codelength are unchanged.
Undirected input that lists a pair in both directions counts it once in the prior's degree.
A tree row whose path is not positive integers separated by ':' is refused (exit 2). Some of these crashed or were misread before.
Hard partitions (library API, clusterDataIsHard): a partition that leaves nodes out stays hard.
Hard partitions (library API, clusterDataIsHard): the run reports the codelength of the tree it returns, and --no-infomap returns the hard modules.
Hard partitions (library API, clusterDataIsHard): the super-level fallback from #1159 also applies.
A ragged seed tree deeper than two levels no longer crashes.
Teleportation to links (not --to-nodes): bipartite input whose links all run from the primary to the feature side is refused with degenerate flow.
undirdir on multilayer input with intra-layer links warns that it has no effect.
State or multilayer input with a seed tree deeper than two levels: every module of the tree gets its physical nodes, so the reported codelength is that of the tree.
Recorded link flow uses the configured teleportation rate. Codelengths move by at most 4e-11, and near-ties can pick another partition.
Directed flow at -p 1: the teleportation rate is kept at or below 1 inside the power iteration, so flow no longer drifts. This can change the search outcome.
With a seed tree deeper than two levels, the reported codelength is that of the returned tree. Best-of-N can pick a different trial.

Bipartite input: teleportation weights are renormalised after the feature nodes are uncoded. Most visible with --to-nodes; teleportation to links changes when the coded nodes have teleportation weight.
Bipartite input: teleportation weights are renormalised after the feature nodes are uncoded, and leaf enter and exit flow come from the links.
Leaf enter and exit flow come from the links. Some runs refused for negative flow before now run.
Markov time other than 1: leaf enter and exit flow come from the links. Most runs at t > 1 were refused before and now run.
Leaf enter and exit flow come from the links. Some runs refused for negative flow before now run.
Hard partitions (library API, clusterDataIsHard) from a .tree, .ftree or JSON path: a one-level tree stays hard, and a deeper tree is refused.
Teleportation to links (not --to-nodes): a network without links is refused with degenerate flow. It used to report a codelength above the one-level codelength.
The scale is floored at an effective degree of 1. Networks with isolated nodes are no longer refused for negative flow.
The scale is floored at an effective degree of 1. Networks with isolated nodes no longer run on negative link flow.
Multilayer input whose expansion is the identity runs first-order: Infomap reads back its own .clu, _states.clu and _states.tree. They were refused for a missing layer id column.
